subject.title: refactor: move MCP OAuth state to SQLite

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the immediate Doctor-only migration contract where legacy MCP OAuth JSON is never read at runtime and existing credentials remain unavailable until an exclusive, verified `doctor --fix` import succeeds?
rationale: This deliberately trades upgrade continuity for a single credential owner and stronger anti-resurrection guarantees; repository policy supports the architecture, but automation cannot choose the acceptable security and operator-impact boundary.

options.title: Approve Doctor-only cutoff
options.body: Accept the single-store contract, verified migration receipts, authoritative logout tombstones, and fail-closed handling as the intended release boundary.

options.title: Require an upgrade grace path
options.body: Delay merge until maintainers define a backward-preserving transition that does not create runtime dual-read, dual-write, or stale-token resurrection.

options.title: Pause the migration
options.body: Keep the existing file store until the operator and credential-security tradeoffs have a different approved design.

recommendation.title: Approve Doctor-only cutoff
recommendation.body: Accept the single-store contract, verified migration receipts, authoritative logout tombstones, and fail-closed handling as the intended release boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly requests this security owner to accept or reject the migration and credential-boundary contract.
